guidelinesCompliance.guideline: Preserve fail-closed behavior and never infer remote absence from a failed deletion request alone.
guidelinesCompliance.evidence: _delete_remote_branch always fetches/prunes and calls _remote_branch_absent; focused failures cover present and unverifiable remote refs.

guidelinesCompliance.guideline: Model closure completion separately from whether the invoking worktree is ready for the next Work Item.
guidelinesCompliance.evidence: close_work_item returns state=closed plus repositoryState, nextWorkItemReady, and baseWorktree; CLI tests reject ready output for detached closure.

guidelinesCompliance.guideline: Do not delete or prune a worktree whose ownership is not established by this Work Item.
guidelinesCompliance.evidence: The command only discovers, checks, and synchronizes the base worktree; neither production code nor real topology tests remove it.

guidelinesCompliance.guideline: Use test-driven development: add failing regressions for each field scenario before changing production behavior.
guidelinesCompliance.evidence: PR Head SHA, mutation order, remote-failure checkout, detach rollback, and terminal-state tests were observed failing against the old implementation before each minimal production change.

guidelinesCompliance.guideline: Keep English and Japanese behavior statements semantically aligned and synchronize the installed ai-cockpit skill only from the merged repository truth.
guidelinesCompliance.evidence: English/Japanese references and Cockpit READMEs use the same exact state names; installed skill synchronization remains explicitly post-merge.

risk.detail: Branch cleanup is intentionally destructive. The approved design preserves local retry identity until remote absence is proven and separates closed state from invoking-worktree readiness.

observedIssues.fact: The implementation plan initially used --cov=scripts.ai_close_work_item, but the test environment imports the script as ai_close_work_item after adding scripts/ to sys.path; pytest therefore passed while coverage emitted module-not-imported and no-data warnings.
observedIssues.decision: Treat warning-only output as insufficient verification, correct the plan to the actual import identity, and rerun the whole focused file with real coverage.
observedIssues.resolution: The corrected --cov=ai_close_work_item run passed 24 tests and measured scripts/ai_close_work_item.py at 77.11% focused coverage without warnings.
observedIssues.followUp: Satisfied by full quality session 9510e88c13ad-local-20260728T134747Z-28568-0; retain the corrected command in the implementation plan.

observedIssues.decision: Keep the failed quality session as evidence, apply the canonical Ruff formatter only to the two named files, rerun all focused closure tests, then restart full quality from the beginning.
observedIssues.resolution: Ruff formatted both files, git diff --check passed, and all 24 focused closure tests passed.
observedIssues.followUp: Satisfied by replacement full quality session 9510e88c13ad-local-20260728T134747Z-28568-0.

observedIssues.fact: After independently running the required gates, manually setting Summary verification results to passed caused check-ai-change-summary to reject every entry because V2 passed results require ai_finish-owned command, timestamp, exit code, output digest, command/Contract/worktree hashes, execution paths, and commit binding.
observedIssues.decision: Do not treat truthful command execution alone as sufficient machine-readable evidence. Restore all verification entries to not_run, refresh the generated checkpoint, and let ai_finish execute and bind every registered check.
observedIssues.resolution: Manual pass claims were removed before archive; no immutable evidence was created from them.
observedIssues.followUp: Require ai_finish-generated provenance and a passing archived Summary before push or PR.
